_readme: Everything identical for every SmartRecruiters customer. A company record under profiles/companies/ names "platform": "smartrecruiters" and adds only what differs: slug, name, careers_url, api.endpoint, detail_fetch.url_template and health.

israel_filter._note: VERIFIED live 2026-08-19 against `fairtility`. post_fetch per SKILL Step 5 - the postings endpoint takes offset/limit but no location parameter, so the whole board arrives and relevance is decided afterwards. `fullLocation` is read in preference to city+country and that choice matters: city+country renders as 'Tel Aviv-Yafo, il', and while every Israeli CITY in the corpus passes relevance, a posting carrying only the country would read as the bare token 'il', which is_relevant_location correctly declines to treat as Israel (it is also Illinois). fullLocation spells it out - 'Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, Israel'. The fetcher falls back to city+country when fullLocation is absent.

api._note: Endpoint: https://api.smartrecruiters.com/v1/companies/{slug}/postings, paginated with offset/limit against `totalFound`. *** A TRAP WORTH KNOWING: this endpoint answers HTTP 200 with {"content": []} for ANY slug, including pure nonsense - checked live against 'thiscompanydoesnotexistatall9x'. *** So a 200 is not evidence a company exists, and discovery must never treat an empty SmartRecruiters board as a hit; see discover_ats.probe_smartrecruiters. Identity IS available, just not where it was first looked for: every posting carries a `company` object with `name`, which is what verified all 12 of this platform's candidates. The posting id is a stable numeric string; the human-facing link is built by api._build_sr_url from the company slug in the endpoint.

detail_fetch._note: VERIFIED live 2026-08-19 against the posting named above. The cheaper rung was checked and ruled out: `inline` is impossible because the LISTING carries only `jobAdId`/`defaultJobAd` identifiers, no description text. The per-posting endpoint returns jobAd.sections as a MAPPING - {companyDescription, jobDescription, qualifications, additionalInformation}, each {title, text} - not the list shape Lever and Comeet use, which is why detail._extract_from_json grew a dict branch. Rendering it through render_sections keeps 'Qualifications' as a real <h3>, and that heading is what promotes the bullets beneath it to mandatory in experience.classify_block - which is the whole point, since qualifications is where the years-of-experience number lives. Costs one GET per NEW posting against the run-wide cap of 40. url_template is per company because the slug is in the path.

health._note: Overridden per company by the importer from that company's live verified count - see the same note in comeet.json.

notes: fetch_smartrecruiters has existed in src/fetchers/api.py since before this file and had never been exercised against a live board by anything in this project - it predated the platform-profile mechanism and no company used it. It is now verified end to end against 12 companies found by the 2026-08-18 sweep, all small Israeli boards (1-6 Israel-relevant postings each). CAVEAT: pagination is therefore confirmed only on boards well under one page. The fetcher's offset/limit loop against `totalFound` is the documented contract and is capped at 50 pages, but 'it paginates correctly' is untested here beyond 100 postings - far weaker evidence than Greenhouse's 437. Re-test before trusting it if a large SmartRecruiters board is ever added.
